title: Argent - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
summary: Follow-up to the incident on 2026-10-01 where Argent experienced increased inference latency and several timeouts. Redwood SE summarized root cause as a combination of autoscaler bounce on Dedicated pool plus KV cache rewarm storm; proposed mitigations include autoscaler patch, async KV rewarm, temporary capacity buffer, and improved observability. Security team confirmed no data exfiltration and SOC2 posture unchanged. Next steps: run focused benchmarks, deploy hotfix to staging, share postmortem doc and updated runbook.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Marcus Hill (CSM), Rajesh Kumar (Argent SRE), Aisha Malik (Argent Head of Platform), Tom Li (Argent VP Eng), Nina Cho (Argent Security)

Summary: quick follow-up after the outage on Oct 1. go over RCA, confirm mitigations, and align next steps.

[00:00] Sam: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we know this has been rough, appreciate the pushback and the details you sent. we'll go through the postmortem takeaways, root cause and the mitigations we've implemented.
[00:22] Rajesh: thanks Sam. quick note, still seeing a couple of elevated p95 traces during the morning window but much reduced vs last week.
[00:30] Lina: yep, and just to be clear up front, the team pushed a hotfix to the autoscaler yesterday and we've been validating on a subset of Dedicated nodes. early indications show the flapping stops when the buffer is enabled.
[00:45] Aisha: can you explain again what the combination of issues was? it sounded like cache + autoscale but i want the concrete flow.
[00:52] Lina: sure — high level we saw three things align: 1) a small spike in request rate during Argent's scheduled batch job led the Dedicated pool autoscaler to spin up a few new instances, 2) during that scale event there was a transient mismatch between the model runtime quant profile and the pre-warmed KV cache causing many requests to miss the cache and rewarm KVs, 3) the rewarm traffic created a short-lived CPU/GPU pressure which triggered additional scaling decisions and some requests timed out while the batcher retried. the retry storm compounded latency.
[01:30] Tom: when you say quant profile mismatch is that from our side or from a Redwood rollout?
[01:38] Lina: it was our canary of a new quantization profile that hit a small subset of nodes; the canary logic should have been isolated but due to a race in the placement service new requests were routed to a node that didn't have the warmed KV entries for that model variant. so it's an internal pathing/placement bug on Redwood.
[02:05] Rajesh: okay that squares with the traces we pulled. we saw cache misses that line up with the scale events.
[02:15] Nina: security question — any impact to tenant data or logs that left Argent's VPC?
[02:21] Marcus: quick answer: no. the incident was resource/latency related and didn't surface any data exfiltration. we've gone back through the audit logs and nothing indicates cross-tenant access. we'll share the audit export to you.
[02:38] Nina: ok thanks, please send that.
[02:42] Sam: high level mitigation we pushed: 1) autoscaler hotfix to avoid aggressive downscaling during rewarm windows, 2) change placement logic so canaries are strictly isolated, 3) make KV rewarm asynchronous and low-priority so it doesn't block generation while warming, and 4) a temporary capacity buffer for Argent's Dedicated pool during your critical windows.
[03:10] Aisha: the buffer — is that manual config or an automated rule?
[03:15] Lina: it's a config toggle for now; we can make it a policy later. we added a 20% buffer for your pool during the 02:00-06:00 ET window where you saw the spike.
[03:28] Tom: what's the ETA for the KV async change?
[03:32] Lina: we've implemented a patch in staging; tests look good. target for canary rollout is 48 hours, full rollout in 5 days if no regressions.
[03:45] Rajesh: are there any other short-term tactics we can use? more aggressive circuit breakers?
[03:50] Lina: yes — we recommend enabling the new circuit-breaker toggle in the route config which will fail fast on persistent misses instead of piling into retries. also we can temporarily increase request timeouts on your side to reduce retry storms, though that's tradeoff with perceived latency.
[04:12] Sam: also we've added a new alert to track KV miss-rate correlated with scale events — that'll surface the pattern quicker.
[04:20] Aisha: good. want to talk about the reliability improvements you mentioned in the doc?
[04:24] Lina: sure. longer term we're adding: improved model variant isolation, stronger canary placement guarantees, delayed downscale windows right after scale-ups, smarter batching backpressure logic, and per-customer warm caches that survive reassignments for a short TTL.
[04:45] Tom: per-customer warm caches — does that consume a lot more memory? will that change pricing or impact other customers?
[04:52] Lina: it does increase memory usage a bit; our plan is to make it configurable per-customer and only for Dedicated pools. for hosted customers we can use a global TTL tuning approach. pricing not changed yet — we'll propose tradeoffs in the write-up.
[05:10] Rajesh: ok we need numbers — how much mem, what latency improvement?
[05:14] Lina: initial microbenchmarks show p95 token latency improvement of ~25% for cache-hit sensitive prompts when cache retention is increased for the hot user set. memory depends on your model size — we'll include a model-by-model table.
[05:30] Nina: any implications for SOC2?
[05:33] Marcus: none. again no cross-tenant data exposure; we're only changing runtime behavior and orchestration. we'll include updated control mapping for the change control log.
[05:45] Sam: next up, questions from your side?
[05:48] Rajesh: a few — can you run the benchmark with our exact prompt set and traffic shape? and can you show us traces after the hotfix?
[05:56] Lina: yes we'll run the Argent benchmark (you sent the prompt set) in staging with the autoscaler patch + async rewarm and share the SDR and flame graphs.
[06:08] Aisha: also want the runbook updated so our on-call knows how to mitigate quickly.
[06:12] Marcus: we'll update the runbook and share a delta. propose a short on-call runthrough next week.
[06:20] Tom: timing — what's the plan for production?
[06:23] Lina: staged canary in 48 hours, if green full rollout in 5 days. the autoscaler hotfix is already in prod for a small percentage and we'll expand it tomorrow.
[06:35] Rajesh: any risk that the autoscaler fix will create over-provisioning and cost surprises?
[06:39] Sam: it's tunable; the current buffer is small (20%) and only during your critical window. we'll work with your finance/ops to estimate cost delta.
[06:50] Aisha: please include cost estimates in the follow-up.
[06:54] Lina: will do.
[06:58] [10:12] Speaker 1: (small cross-talk and side conversations)
[10:30] Lina: quick note — we found that the retry logic in the batcher was doubling retries in some failure cases; patching that reduces retry amplification.
[11:00] Rajesh: excellent. also, is there a way to get more granular observability on KV heatmaps?
[11:07] Lina: yes we're adding a KV heatmap dashboard that shows per-model, per-tenant hit rates over time. we'll give access to Argent dashboards.
[11:20] Nina: please include the audit export Marcus mentioned.
[11:23] Marcus: sending after the call.
[11:28] Sam: ok let's recap; root cause: placement/canary race + KV rewarm causing resource pressure leading to scale flapping & retries. mitigations: autoscaler hotfix, async KV rewarm, circuit-breaker toggle, temporary capacity buffer, batcher retry fix, enhanced dashboards. next steps we agreed: benchmarks, runbook update, audit export, cost estimate, canary schedule.
[11:55] Aisha: sounds good. thanks for the clear plan.
[12:00] Tom: appreciate it — please send the postmortem doc and we'll schedule the run-through.
[12:08] Sam: will do, expect the postmortem and the mitigation plan plus timelines by EOD tomorrow.
[12:15] Rajesh: thanks all.
[12:18] (call ends)
